author: Madelyn Amos
title: Millions Lose SNAP Benefits as New Federal Law Tightens Access to Food Assistance
content:
Millions of Americans are losing access to food assistance as new federal restrictions on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) take effect across the country.

According to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP), more than 4.5 million people have lost SNAP benefits since the Republican budget law was enacted in July 2025. By April 2026, national SNAP enrollment had fallen by about 11%, marking one of the steepest declines in the program’s history.

The law expanded work requirements and made it more difficult for many people to qualify for or maintain benefits. While supporters argue the changes encourage employment and reduce federal spending, advocates warn that many people losing assistance are already working, face barriers to employment, or care for children or family members.

The cuts come as many families continue to struggle with the high cost of groceries and other essentials. Anti-hunger organizations report that food banks and community pantries are experiencing increased demand as households that lose SNAP benefits seek emergency assistance. However, advocates emphasize that charitable food programs cannot replace the scale and reliability of the federal nutrition program.

author: Madelyn Amos
title: The Democratic Women’s Caucus Honors Women Who Serve Despite Political Backlash
content:
This year’s annual Women in Military Service Wreath- Laying Ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery looked different than in the past years. The event, hosted by the Bipartisan Women’s Caucus for 28 years, was canceled after several military branches declined to participate.

According to multiple officials, the decision stemmed from President Trump’s Executive Order 14185 , which seeks to eliminate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) programs across the federal government. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth reinforced the policy by issuing guidance titled “ Identity Months Dead at DoD ,” prohibiting the DoD and military branches from using official resources to host celebrations recognizing race, gender, or other identity groups.

In response, the Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC), led by Vice Chair Rep. Emilia Sykes (OH-13), organized its own event to honor women veterans.

On June 10, 2026, members of the DWC gathered on Capitol Hill for a joint press conference recognizing the service and sacrifice of women in the military, paying tribute to both fallen servicewomen and living veterans.

Sykes criticized the administration’s decision, saying, “at a time when veterans should be celebrated, the Trump-Hegseth Pentagon is sidelining them.” She also pledged that the DWC would continue working to recognize and support women who have served.
